aria: Animated recap of the Nuggets' 105 to 101 comeback win over Boston: Jamal Murray's 17-foot jumper with 6.4 seconds left, quarter-by-quarter scoring after a 17-point deficit, Nikola Jokić's 24 points, 9 assists and 8 rebounds, the top scorers, how Denver won, and Friday's game against Houston.
notes: Box score from the Denver Nuggets' 105–101 win over the Boston Celtics at Ball Arena on Nov 18, 2026, from the Covers box score, with the lines checked against the Associated Press (via Denver7) and game details from the Boston Globe, Denver Stiffs, DenverSports.com, Field Level Media (via JOX FM), MassLive (via Yahoo Sports) and Yardbarker. All 105 Denver points and all 101 Boston points are accounted for, and the quarter scores add up to both totals: Boston 30–24 after one, 61–49 at the half, tied 80–80 after three. The AP story matches the Covers lines for Jokić (24, 8 rebounds, 9 assists), Murray (21, 7 rebounds, 4 steals), DeRozan (18), Queta (17 and 10) and Pritchard (15), and Boston's 11 of 44 from three. Field goals (37 of 85 to 40 of 98), threes (7 of 31 to 11 of 44), free throws (24 of 29 to 10 of 12), fast-break points (18–14), points in the paint (34–48) and the biggest leads (Boston 17, Denver 4) are from Covers; the fouls (Boston 30, Denver 13) also from MassLive. Records and ranks are from the site's standings after Wednesday's games.

Boston led 61–44 late in the second quarter on a Jayson Tatum three (DenverSports.com; Field Level Media). In the third, Boston turned it over on eight straight possessions and Denver went ahead 69–67 on a Cameron Johnson jumper (Boston Globe; AP). The teams traded the lead 15 times in the final 16:10 (AP). DeMar DeRozan scored 13 of his 18 in the fourth (AP). Neemias Queta's putback put Boston up 101–100 with 1:06 left; DeRozan's two free throws with 49 seconds left gave Denver the lead for good, 102–101 (AP; Boston Globe; Field Level Media). Jamal Murray's jumper with 6.4 seconds left made it 104–101, and he made the technical free throw after Tatum was called for one (AP; Boston Globe). Denver has won five of its last seven (AP). The Nuggets host Houston on Friday (AP; the site's schedule).

The play of the game is an original illustration of Jamal Murray's 17-foot pull-up jumper with 6.4 seconds left that put Denver up 104–101 (AP and the Boston Globe give the clock and the score; DenverSports.com and Yardbarker describe it as a 17-foot pull-up). It is drawn as the template's pull-up from the elbow. The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The music is an original beat made for this page. No existing recordings or melodies are used. This is an unofficial fan recap, not affiliated with the Denver Nuggets or the NBA, which is why it carries a plain basketball mark and the team's colors but not the team's logo.

The shooter in the play of the game is drawn to Murray's listed 6-foot-4 and 215 pounds (RealGM), with his arms scaled to a reported 6-foot-7 wingspan (CraftedNBA), in Denver's home white with No. 27 (RealGM). He has no approved look on file yet, so he is drawn in the kit with the default skin tone. It is an original figure with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
